forbidden_claims.reason: root theorem proposition is not citable solver context
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, ℓ with 0 ≤ k, ℓ ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose ℓ]_q is a polynomial in q, then it has only nonnegative coefficients.

payload.role_in_assembly: Moves each lower index to the first half of [0,n] without changing the quotient.

domain_restrictions: Therefore n is automatically a nonnegative integer.
The quantities (q;q)_r, (q;q)_{n-r}, and (q;q)_n are only formed for nonnegative integer indices.
q is treated as a formal indeterminate, not as a quantified numeric variable.
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every pair of integers n and r with 0 <= r <= n, the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient is symmetric under replacing r by n-r; that is, the coefficient defined by the q-factorial ratio for r equals the one defined for n-r, as a polynomial in q.
quantifier_order: For all integers n and r, assume 0 <= r <= n.
For each nonnegative integer m, define (q;q)_m by the stated finite product, with (q;q)_0 equal to 1.
Then the q-binomial coefficient defined from these q-factorials satisfies the symmetry identity.
The equality is asserted as an identity of polynomials in q.

payload.statement_nl: For all integers n and r with 0 <= r <= n, define the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient by [n choose r]_q := (q;q)_n / ((q;q)_r (q;q)_{n-r}), where (q;q)_m := product_{i=1}^m (1 - q^i) and (q;q)_0 := 1. Then [n choose r]_q = [n choose n-r]_q as polynomials in q.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Fix integers n and r with 0 <= r <= n. Then r >= 0 and n-r >= 0, so both quantities [n choose r]_q and [n choose n-r]_q are defined by the given formula

[n choose s]_q := (q;q)_n / ((q;q)_s (q;q)_{n-s})

for the relevant values s=r and s=n-r.

Now compute directly from the definition:

[n choose n-r]_q
= (q;q)_n / ((q;q)_{n-r} (q;q)_{n-(n-r)})
= (q;q)_n / ((q;q)_{n-r} (q;q)_r).

Since multiplication is commutative,

(q;q)_{n-r} (q;q)_r = (q;q)_r (q;q)_{n-r}.

Therefore

[n choose n-r]_q
= (q;q)_n / ((q;q)_r (q;q)_{n-r})
= [n choose r]_q.

So the two defining expressions are identical. Hence the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient is symmetric under replacing r by n-r; in particular, [n choose r]_q = [n choose n-r]_q as polynomials in q.
result_payload.proof_summary: Using only the definition, replace r by n-r and note that n-(n-r)=r. The denominator becomes (q;q)_{n-r}(q;q)_r, which equals (q;q)_r(q;q)_{n-r} by commutativity, so the expressions are identical.
